This shape holds 1210-1211; empire-of-trebizond_1212 takes over for 1212-1214 and _1215 from 1215. Sudak was Seljuk 1220-1222, so the Perateia part should exclude it then.

Oinaion was Trapezuntine 1228-1230 and from 1243, Seljuk between; the oscillation is under 50 km. Mongol vassal from 1243. The Crimean part (Perateia) was by now ruled by the Gabras family under weak Trapezuntine suzerainty: draw as vassal tint if the renderer allows.

ledger.note: 'Alexios took possession of Limnia, Samsun and Sinope.' Counterpart is the collapsing Byzantine provincial administration.

region.text: coastal Paphlagonia: Heraclea Pontica (Eregli), Tios, Amastris (Amasra) and the Kastamonu hinterland, David Komnenos' conquests of 1204

ledger.note: 1204: Theodore I Laskaris page, the paragraph on Sept-Dec 1204: 'David Komnenos launched a military campaign into Paphlagonia and occupied the towns along the Black Sea coast' (no town named there). Towns and region are my reading of two other pages, re-read 2026-10-19: Alexios I of Trebizond, 'David proceeded along the coast, perhaps leading a fleet, capturing Kerasous, Cide, Amasra and Heraclea Pontica' (so that sentence is on the Alexios I page, not on the David Komnenos page, where the earlier note looked for it); David Komnenos, 'aided by Georgian troops and local mercenaries, made himself master of Pontus and Paphlagonia' and 'the cities of Amastris, Tios and Heraclea Pontica all welcomed him' (undated there). Confidence 2: the year is the Theodore page's; the extent (Heraclea Pontica to the Kastamonu hinterland) is a reading.

region.text: Perateia: the southern Crimean coast from Cherson to Kerch, a tributary overseas province

ledger.note: Perateia (Cherson, Kerch and hinterlands) 'made... a tributary to Trebizond'; 'Trapezuntine control over Perateia had been weak almost from the beginning'. The counterpart slug stands for the local Gabras-ruled Gothia that later became Theodoro; its Cliopatria row only begins in 1333.

region.text: Trebizond and the province of Chaldia, occupied by Alexios and David Komnenos in April 1204 with Queen Tamar's help

ledger.note: 'In April 1204, while Constantinople was occupied with the on-going conflict with the Fourth Crusade, David and Alexios occupied the city of Trebizond'; 'Immediately that city, Oinaion and Sinope declared for the two brothers.' (David Komnenos page; re-read 2026-10-19, the earlier version cited the Alexios I page, which does not contain the second sentence.)
Unsuccessful Seljuk siege of Trebizond 'around the year 1205' (David page: 1205 or 1206).

region.text: Heraclea Pontica and Amastris, David's western march

ledger.note: 1208: David Komnenos page, 'In 1208 Laskaris renewed his offensive against David Komnenos' and 'invested Heraclea Pontica'; Henry of Flanders then occupied Nicomedia and Laskaris lifted the siege. Alexios I of Trebizond page: 'In 1208 Theodore decided to strike against the Paphlagonian possessions of Alexios' brother David'. The Theodore I Laskaris page has an earlier 1206 decision to take Heraclea Pontica that a Latin attack on his army cut short, with no ground taken; the contest starts with the first campaign that holds ground (1208), and nicaean-empire /ledger/5 is moved to 1208 to agree.

region.text: Heraclea Pontica (Eregli), Tios, Amastris (Amasra) and the western Paphlagonian coast to 32.6E

ledger.note: Battle of Antioch on the Meander page: 'in 1212, the death of David Komnenos allowed their annexation of his lands in Paphlagonia' (David died 13 December 1212, David Komnenos page). Alexios I of Trebizond page: 'Theodore eventually captured Heraclea Pontica and Amastris' (undated). Region split on 2026-10-19 to agree with nicaean-empire /ledger/13 (31-32.6E); the eastern part, 32.6E to the Sinope district, is the 1214 loss below. The pages disagree whether all of Paphlagonia went in 1212 (Antioch page) or in late 1214 (Treaty of Nymphaeum page: 'Theodore was thus able to annex all of David's lands west of Sinope in late 1214'); the 1212/1214 split is the compromise both dossiers use.

region.text: eastern Paphlagonia west of the Sinope district: Kastamonu, Cide, Inebolu, to about 34.4E

ledger.note: Empire of Trebizond page: 'the territories west of Sinope were lost to Theodore I Laskaris by 1214'. Treaty of Nymphaeum (1214) page: Theodore 'was thus able to annex all of David's lands west of Sinope in late 1214'. Theodore I Laskaris page: Theodore and Kaykaus I 'invaded the Empire of Trebizond simultaneously in 1214' and 'whether he conquered eastern Paphlagonia during this campaign, or only years later, is unclear'. The east edge (about 34.4E) is the west edge of the Sinope district, which went to the Seljuks on 1 November 1214 (next event); added 2026-10-19 to match nicaean-empire /ledger/14. Confidence 2: 'by 1214' is the page's bound, the exact year within it is not.

region.text: Heraclea, Amastris and Paphlagonia west of Sinope, the zone fought over 1208-1214

ledger.note: Empire of Trebizond page: 'the territories west of Sinope were lost to Theodore I Laskaris by 1214'; moved from 1212 on 2026-10-19 to agree with nicaean-empire /ledger/15 (1214), the year the last Paphlagonian land west of Sinope went.

Siege of Sinope page: the city 'surrendered on 1 November' (infobox 1 November 1214) and, 'apart from a period of Trapezuntine recovery in 1254-1265, the city henceforth remained in Turkish hands'. Alexios I of Trebizond page (second page): Alexios was 'captured by the Turks in the field while defending Sinope'; 'on 1 November 1214 the inhabitants surrendered their city to the Seljuks on terms'. The frontier wording 'back to the Iris and Thermodon rivers' is on that Alexios I page, not on the Siege of Sinope page (the earlier note cited the wrong page and said 'back toward'); see the next event.

region.text: the coast between the Sinope district and the Iris mouth: Bafra, Samsun (Amisos)

ledger.note: Alexios I of Trebizond page: 'The loss of Sinope pushed the western frontier of Komnenine territories, which had been at Heraclea a few years earlier, back to the Iris and Thermodon rivers, only 250 kilometres (160 mi) from their base at Trebizond'; the same page has Alexios taking 'Limnia, Samsun and Sinope' in 1204. Samsun lies west of the Iris mouth (about 36.6E), so it went with Sinope; the page does not name Samsun or Bafra in 1214, so the region is my reading (confidence 2). Added 2026-10-19 after the review (the Sinope disc alone left Samsun Trapezuntine against the frontier at the Iris). Cliopatria's 1210 shape already starts at about 36.7E and has no cell at Samsun.
Seljuk siege of Trebizond 1222-1223, broken by a storm during the night assault.

region.text: Perateia: the southern Crimean coast from Cherson to Kerch, a tributary overseas province

ledger.note: 'In 1223 the Seljuk governor of Sinope sent ships to attack the coast of Trapezuntine Crimea'; Andronikos sent a fleet against Sinope. Sudak had been Seljuk since 1220-1222.
Oinaion Trapezuntine 1228-1230.

region.text: the Georgian dependencies ('Iberia and Lazica') east of the Chorokhi, which 'separated themselves from the empire and formed an independent kingdom of Imereti'

ledger.note: A Fallmerayer-era claim repeated on the Andronikos I page; the extent of any Trapezuntine Lazica is unknown and the Cliopatria shapes never reach beyond Batumi. Year is a placeholder within 1222-1235.
Oinaion Trapezuntine 1243-1297.
'On 24 June 1254, Manuel recaptured Sinope, and made Ghadras archon of the Black Sea port', under an Ilkhanid yarligh.
'Permanent loss of Sinope: 1265' (to the Pervane Mu'in al-Din Suleiman, nominally Seljuk).

region.text: 'several provinces' of the eastern empire, occupied by David VI Narin of Imereti while John II was in Constantinople

ledger.note: 'Though King David failed to take the city, the Georgians occupied several provinces.' Which provinces is not stated; the eastern coast is the reading. Imereti has no Cliopatria row before 1468.

Treaty of 1282 with Michael VIII: John II gave up 'Emperor and Autocrat of the Romans' for 'Emperor and Autocrat of all the East, the Iberians, and the Transmarine Provinces'. No territory changed; the state and colour continue.

region.text: the eastern provinces occupied by the Georgians in 1282

ledger.note: End of the Georgian occupation is not dated; assumed within a year.

region.text: Chalybia, the coast and hinterland around Ordu/Fatsa between Oinaion and Kerasous

ledger.note: Panaretos: 'during his reign the Turks seized Chalybia and launched a great invasion, so that all those places became uninhabited' (John II, 1280-1297); year a midpoint. The Turkmen beys of Chalybia (later the Haciemiroglu) have no Cliopatria row; the nominal Seljuk slug is used.

Haciemiroglu 1297-1302. John II built the Unye fortress 'on the western border' in the 1290s and died at Limnia in 1297; 'the thirteen towns or forts of Limnia' remained. [Reviewer eu-05-d, 2026-10-19: counterpart was 'sultanate-of-rum'; the Oinaion page gives the town to the 'Emirate of Hacıemiroğlu between 1297-1302 and 1346–1461' and never names the Ottomans or the Seljuks for these years; named as the page gives it (suggested slug haciemiroglu, in the author's counterparts_needing_dossiers).]

Oinaion Trapezuntine 1302-1346; Alexios II 'defeated a Turkoman invasion' that had sacked Kerasous in 1301 or 1302 and fortified the town. [Reviewer eu-05-d, 2026-10-19: counterpart was 'sultanate-of-rum'; the Oinaion page gives the town to the 'Emirate of Hacıemiroğlu between 1297-1302 and 1346–1461' and never names the Ottomans or the Seljuks for these years; named as the page gives it (suggested slug haciemiroglu, in the author's counterparts_needing_dossiers).]

region.text: the Genoese quarter at Daphnous and the suburbs of Trebizond

ledger.note: Genoese demands refused 1306; fighting in which 'the Genoese set fire to the suburbs of Trebizond'; peace treaties 1314 and 1316.

region.text: the Genoese quarter and suburbs of Trebizond
Perateia: the southern Crimean coast from Cherson to Kerch, a tributary overseas province

ledger.note: Cliopatria's convention: Crimea leaves the Trebizond row and the Theodoro row begins in 1333. In fact Trapezuntine authority over Gothia had been nominal since the 1220s and the Gabras princes ruled under the Golden Horde.

'Emirate of Haciemiroglu between 1297-1302 and 1346-1461'; main page 1347-48 'conquering Oinaion and besieging Trebizond'. The Haciemiroglu beylik has no Cliopatria row; the Ottoman slug (Cliopatria's neighbour from 1344) is a placeholder and should be replaced if a Chalybia/Haciemiroglu dossier is created. [Reviewer eu-05-d, 2026-10-19: counterpart was 'ottoman-empire'; the Oinaion page gives the town to the 'Emirate of Hacıemiroğlu between 1297-1302 and 1346–1461' and never names the Ottomans or the Seljuks for these years; named as the page gives it (suggested slug haciemiroglu, in the author's counterparts_needing_dossiers).]
'the Genoese seized Kerasus' (1347-1348).

Genoese hold of Kerasous ended with 'the concession of Leonkastron to the Genoese in 1349' (a fort at Trebizond); by 1354 Kerasous was the base of the rebel megas doux Niketas, retaken by Alexios III in May 1355.

region.text: Leonkastron, the fort and quay west of Trebizond ceded to Genoa

ledger.note: Sub-cell; recorded for completeness.

ledger.counterpart: Niketas Scholares and the Scholarioi rebels
ledger.note: Alexios III page: 'By June 1354 the megas doux was forced to flee to Kerasous', where he prepared a fleet; the rebels sailed against Trebizond in March 1355 but 'abandoned their expedition'. Replaces the 1340-1349 whole-empire contest that named the state itself as counterpart (review of 2026-10-19): the Empire of Trebizond page names the factions (Scholaroi, 'pro-Byzantine', and Amytzantarantes, 'native archontes') and the Alexios III page says only that the preceding decade was 'distracted ... by the jealousies and ambitions of rival gangs of noble place-hunters', so no ground held by a faction before 1354 is documented. Confidence 2: 'by June 1354' is a bound.

region.text: the Matzouka and upper Philabonites valleys, the frontier against the Turkmen

ledger.note: Alexios III 'suffered a major defeat in battle in 1355' while 'strengthening the frontier against the Turkmen'; no town named; Aq Qoyunlu (Cliopatria row from 1407) stands for the Turkmen of Bayburt. Low confidence placeholder.

ledger.counterpart: Niketas Scholares and the Scholarioi rebels
ledger.note: Alexios III page: 'In May 1355' the emperor 'conquered the town in the absence of Niketas'; his cavalry then besieged 'the last fortress loyal to the megas doux, Kenchrina' (location not given, so not drawn) and obtained its surrender; Niketas 'died in 1360' in Trebizond.

region.text: Limnia, the westernmost Trapezuntine district around the mouth of the Yesilirmak (Iris), with its thirteen forts, and Oinaion (Unye)

ledger.note: 'Between the two dates [1384 and 1386], Limnia irrevocably slipped from Trapezuntine control and became a Turkoman possession' (Tajeddin, emir of Limnia, husband of Alexios III's daughter Eudokia since 8 October 1379). Counterpart placeholder as for 1346. [Reviewer eu-05-d, 2026-10-19: counterpart was 'ottoman-empire'; the Limnia (Pontus) page says Limnia 'became a Turkoman possession' with Tajeddin Çelebi as Emir of Limnia in 1386 and does not mention the Ottomans.]
Siege 14 September 1460 - 15 August 1461 (infobox dates); 'On 15 August 1461, Sultan Mehmed II entered Trebizond'; Mesochaldia submitted to Hizir; Bryer: pockets resisted up to ten years.

wars.outcome: Trapezuntine victory; vassalage to Iconium ended

belligerents: Niketas Scholares and the Scholarioi rebels

Only the 1354-55 rebellion has documented ground (Kerasous, Kenchrina): see the ledger contest pair; the 1340-1349 strife between the Scholaroi and the Amytzantarantes (Empire of Trebizond page) has no ground the pages opened name, so no contest is drawn for it. The dedicated Wikipedia page would not load.

certainty.note: A coastal strip whose inland edge is the Pontic watershed; the western frontier (Thermodon, Oinaion, Limnia) moved with Turkmen pressure and is dated by single mentions.

sources.title: Gazaria (Genoese colonies)
sources.note: Genoese Crimea (Caffa, Soldaia 1365, Cembalo).

sources.title: Treaty of Nymphaeum (1214)
sources.note: December 1214 Latin-Nicaean treaty that omits David Komnenos, so his Paphlagonian lands were gone by then.

sources.title: Theodore I Laskaris
sources.note: 1204 David Komnenos campaign into Paphlagonia; 1206 decision to take Heraclea Pontica, interrupted by the Latins; 1214 campaign against Trebizond.

sources.title: Battle of Antioch on the Meander
sources.note: "in 1212, the death of David Komnenos allowed their annexation of his lands in Paphlagonia".

notes:
Cliopatria rows: the Empire of Trebizond row (1206-1462) starts two years late (April 1204) and ends a year late (15 August 1461); new keyframes 1204 (with Paphlagonia to Heraclea), 1215 (after the loss of Sinope) and 1254 (second Sinope, 1254-1265) are proposed. The 1206-1332 shapes include the Crimean Perateia (bbox to 44.78N), which Cliopatria drops in 1333 when its Principality of Theodoro row begins; the Perateia page says Trapezuntine control 'had been weak almost from the beginning' and that the Gabras family administered it after 1223, so the Crimea part is best drawn as a vassal tint from the 1220s and the vassal_start/end events (counterpart principality-of-theodoro, whose row does not exist before 1333) record that. The 1344 shape doubles the area (13,617 to 26,606 km2) by adding an inland band to 40.03N exactly when the Ilkhanate row ends (1343); Bayburt and the Kelkit valley were Turkmen, so every 1344-1462 shape is marked adjust back to the 1333 coastal outline, minus Oinaion (1346) and Limnia (1384-86). Rule 2: the 1282 title change is a rename, not a new state.

Suzerains of Trebizond (rule 4; to be recorded as vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart empire-of-trebizond by the suzerain's dossier, since this dossier may only record its own vassals): Kingdom of Georgia, client 1204-1227 (infobox); Sultanate of Rum, tributary 1 November 1214 - 1223 (siege of Sinope; ended by the pact after the failed siege of 1222-23) and again 1230 - 1243 (after Yassicemen; c. 1240 the ruler sent 200 lances); Mongol Empire / Ilkhanate 1243-1335 (infobox 'vassal of the Mongol Empire (1243-1335)'; Manuel I at Guyuk's court 1246; Sinope recovered 1254 under an Ilkhanid yarligh); Timurid Empire, nominal 1402-1405; Ottoman Empire, tribute from c. 1456 to the conquest of 1461. Trebizond's own vassal was Perateia (Crimea), recorded in the ledger.

Counterpart placeholders: the Turkmen beys of Chalybia/Haciemiroglu (1297-1302, 1346-1461) and the emirs of Limnia (Tajeddin) have no Cliopatria row; the 1285 event uses sultanate-of-rum as a placeholder; the 1297, 1302 and 1346 Oinaion events name the 'Emirate of Hacıemiroğlu' (Oinaion page; suggested slug haciemiroglu) and the 1385 Limnia event the 'Emirate of Limnia' (Limnia page), both set by the reviewer on 2026-10-19, and the 1354-55 Kerasous rebellion names 'Niketas Scholares and the Scholarioi rebels'; re-point them if dossiers are written. Kingdom of Imereti (David VI Narin's siege of 1282) has no row before 1468; kingdom-of-georgia is used. Pages that would not load: 'Trapezuntine Civil War'. Disagreements: Sinope lost 1214 (all pages) but the Alexios I lead says he was captured 'in the field while defending Sinope' and the body 'while besieging'; Oinaion lost 1346 (Oinaion page) or 1347-48 (main page); Mongol submission 1243 (main page) vs. 1246 attendance at Guyuk's court (Kose Dag page); Imereti separation from Trebizond (Andronikos I page) is a 19th-century reading. Area sanity: the coastal strip from the Yesilirmak to Batumi at 20-40 km depth is 12,000-16,000 km2, matching the 1210-1333 shapes once Perateia is subtracted.

Gazetteer names used as coordinates because the gazetteer lacks them: Unye/Oinaion, Limnia, Amastris (Amasra), Chalybia, Leonkastron, Matzouka, Caffa, Cembalo; Heraclea Pontica is drawn around Eregli; Kerasous around Giresun.

Repairs of 2026-10-19 after the eu-05-d review (Paphlagonia timeline, agreed with nicaean-empire): 1204 David's Paphlagonian campaign dated from the Theodore I Laskaris page (confidence 2); contest 1208-1214 (start 1208 agreed with Nicaea, end moved from 1212 to 1214); loss of Heraclea Pontica and Amastris 1212 (31-32.6E, Antioch on the Meander page) and of eastern Paphlagonia 1214 (32.6-34.4E, Empire of Trebizond page 'by 1214'; Nymphaeum page 'late 1214'); Sinope loss (1 November 1214) kept with the Iris/Thermodon quote re-sourced to the Alexios I page, and the coast to the Iris (Bafra, Samsun) added as its own event; keyframes: _1210 now holds 1210-1211 with Sinope and Paphlagonia, new _1212 holds 1212-1214, _1215 loses the coast to the Iris. The Cliopatria 1210 shape was checked cell by cell against the gazetteer: it has no cell at Samsun, one in the Sinope disc and starts at 36.7E, so it is the post-1214 frontier. The 1340-1349 whole-empire contest (counterpart the state itself) was dropped for lack of documented ground and replaced by the 1354-55 Kerasous rebellion pair.
